# APK Virtual Machine — a DeepSeek Harness plugin
**Run a real Android APK inside a local, rooted, open-source Android VM and preview it in the DeepSe
ek Harness sidebar — streamed as H.264/WebCodecs video at up to 60 fps.**
Real panel capture: rooted Android 14 guest, live H.264 stream, input controls and installed-app too
ure: rooted Android 14 guest, live H.264 stream, input controls and installed-app tools — no mockup.
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-apk-vm
reproducible demo
**Why it is useful**

- **Sidebar-first Android** — install and use an APK without opening a separate emulator window.
- *

*Real, low-latency stream** — H.264/WebCodecs up to 60 fps with tap, swipe, key and text input.
- **
Agent-native** — `apk_vm` tools, a live UI Inspector, copy-ready selectors and record/replay flows.
- **Local and inspectable** — open-source AOSP emulator, rooted debug API, network/storage controls,

no telemetry.
- **Expandable viewer** — turn the narrow sidebar panel into a full-window VM with on

e click; Escape restores it.
- **Large-screen controls** — collapsible tools, quality presets (540p/
30 → 960p/60), double-click expand, quick rotate, and a stale-UI/version warning.

This repository contains the static DSH plugin `dsh-apk-vm`. It adds a first-class sidebar
entry ("A

PK Virtual Machine" / "APK 虚拟机") whose main panel boots an AOSP Android Emulator,
installs an APK in

to the guest, streams the guest display into the panel, and forwards
tap / swipe / key / text input

back into the VM. The guest is a `userdebug` image prepared for
root (`adb root` on every boot), and

the plugin exposes that rooted device to DSH through a
same-origin, loopback-only debug HTTP API an
d an `apk_vm` Agent tool.

> **中文简介**：在 DeepSeek Harness 的侧边栏里预览 Android APK。插件会启动本地开源
[该节后续省略]
## Risks, permissions and compatibility
**Requirements**

- Android SDK with `adb`, emulator, `sdkmanager`/`avdmanager`, a matching system image and an AVD
(t

he Environment card checks all of this; SDK bootstrap is opt-in).
- Hardware virtualization: AEHD/WH

PX on Windows, KVM on Linux, or HVF on macOS.
- Node.js ≥ 20 only for the repository's headless chec

ks; the plugin itself has no npm
dependencies or build step.
- Each running VM costs roughly 2.5 GB
RAM; `maxInstances` defaults to 3 extra VMs.
**Permissions / risk**

- The guest is intentionally `userdebug` and rooted (`adb root` on boot); do not put secrets or
pers

onal data in the AVD.
- `apk_vm` is registered for every Agent in the profile and exposes guest root

shell, app
install/uninstall, UIAutomator and input injection. Grant it the same trust as a termina

l on a
rooted Android device.
- `/apk-vm/*` HTTP routes and WebSocket upgrades are same-origin and *

*loopback-only by
default**; `allowRemote: true` is an explicit opt-in for use behind a trusted auth

enticated
proxy.
- No telemetry. Network access only occurs for explicit SDK/system-image downloads

through the
user's `sdkmanager`, or when the user configures a remote adb device.
**Compatibility**

- Tested with DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.3` (static bundle/plugin APIs).
- Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 (

headless, KVM + SwiftShader) are verified end-to-end
(boot, H.264, rooted debug, APK install, Agent

tool). macOS has SDK discovery + headless CI
coverage but no live emulator run in this repository.
S

ee docs/LINUX-E2E.md.
- Optional integration with
`dsh-better-sidebar`; the plugin falls back
cleanl

y when that service is absent.
- AOSP Android 14 / API 34, x86_64 system image; physical/remote adb

devices can be attached
instead of the AVD.
### 1. Prerequisites
| Requirement | Notes |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | A profile that can install local plugin bundles (the desktop Web UI or any

agent with the `plugin_manager` tool). |
| **Android SDK** | `platform-tools` (adb), `emulator`, `bu
ild-tools` (for `aapt2`), command-line tools (`sdkmanager`/`avdmanager`) and an AOSP system image. A

JDK (17 works) is needed by the SDK command-line tools. |
| **AOSP system image** | `system-images;
android-34;default;x86_64` (Android 14, API 34) — the image used for all measurements below. Configu

rable with `systemImage`. |
| **Hardware virtualization** | Required for the x86_64 image: AEHD or W

HPX on Windows, KVM on Linux, HVF on macOS. See acceleration matrix. |
| **Disk / RAM** | A few GB f

or the SDK + system image and the AVD; an emulator with a modern desktop GPU is recommended. |
| **N
ode.js 24+** *(optional)* | Only for running this repository's checks (Verification). The plugin its
elf has no npm dependencies. |

The plugin's **Environment** card performs this check for you (see
First run); the commands below ar
e the manual equivalent.
## Compatibility with dsh-better-sidebar

dsh-better-sidebar is the community sidebar
workbench (right-sidebar tabs, bottom workbench, file vi

ewers). When it is active, this plugin
registers a real tab type through its documented service — no

forks, no DOM hacks, no hard
dependency:

- The client half defers with `ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'], …)`, so the plugin keeps working
unchan

ged on a plain DSH and simply gains the tab when the service appears.
- `ctx.betterSidebar.registerT

ab({ id: 'apk-vm:preview', title, description, icon, order: 60,
single: true, component })` — the ta

b appears in the native right Sidebar's **+** menu and in
the bottom workbench, rendered with the sa

me VM console adapted to a narrow pane (stacked APK
list, compact header, `visible`-gated frame poll

ing).
- The main panel gains an **"Open in side bar"** action that calls
`ctx.betterSidebar.openTab(

{ type: 'apk-vm:preview', target: 'right' })` for the active
session (with a clear message when no s

ession is open).
- Everything degrades cleanly: the service is optional, and a missing/broken servic

e never
affects the native `main` panel or the left sidebar entry.

Live-verified in the reference profile: the `sidebar.right.pane.tab` slot lists the occupant
`dsh-be

tter-sidebar:apk-vm:preview` (`active: true`). The sandbox test
spike/ui-better-sidebar-smoke.cjs se

parately asserts
descriptor fields, localization, disposal, the "already present" path, and resilien

ce when the
service disappears.
